payload.summary: Maor Bril argues that video generation has improved much faster than video evaluation, so the real bottleneck is deciding whether a clip is coherent rather than producing one. His approach combines frame-level signals, a fast vision-language judge, and human calibration into a repeatable benchmark, then moves that evaluation as close to generation as possible so drift, physics mistakes, and audio mismatches are caught earlier and cheaper. A major design choice is to prefer pairwise comparisons and carefully constructed training data over absolute scoring, because the first judge version learned visual gloss and AI-versus-real artifacts instead of true quality. The practical consequence is a production-friendly eval wall that can explain why a clip is bad, not just whether it is bad.
